Definition: of uncertain derivation; a fox, i.e. (figuratively) a cunning person:--fox.
BiblicalUsage: A fox, and Jesus uses it twice. Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head. And to Herod He sends a message: Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected; the word is the cunning animal, and in the second use it is the cunning king.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for a fox carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the two sayings, that the Son of man had less shelter than a fox and that a fox of a king could not stop His work.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
